newsitem.title: CROATIA: Party nominates Tudjman for presidential candidate.
newsitem.headline: Party nominates Tudjman for presidential candidate.

text.p: Croatia's ruling party formally nominated President Franjo Tudjman on Sunday as its candidate for a presidential election due later this year.
The announcement, read out at the annual congress of the Croatian Democratic Union (HDZ) in Zagreb, received a standing ovation.
Shortly before his candidacy was made official the autocratic, 75-year old president made an hour-long speech and embarked on a tirade against opponents of his party.

"We cannot understand, even less justify, the siding with the anti-HDZ harangue, of those political parties that should naturally be close to the HDZ," he said. "It can only be a sign of their political immaturity".

Tudjman, reported to be ill with cancer, will run for his third term in office. As founder and leader of the HDZ he won the first democratic election in 1990, shortly before Croatia seceded from communist Yugoslavia.
He was treated at a U.S. hospital near Washington last November for what U.S. sources said was terminal stomach cancer. On his return he looked weak and noticeably thinner than before.
He underwent further treatment at home under the supervision of Western medical experts and now appears in good health, though still thinner then before.

Some diplomats have estimated Tudjman's worsening health might yet force him to give up his duty but he vigorously denied it in an interview with the television network CNN last month and stressed he was feeling good enough to run for president again.
The date for the election has not been set yet. But few observers see a potential challenger for the widely popular president who steered Croatia through a war with minority Serbs to independence.

Regional and local elections throughout Croatia are scheduled for April 13. The HDZ's popularity, maintained only by Tudjman's charisma, is declining over popular discontent with corruption and economic mismanagement.
In his address Tudjman appealed to the HDZ to "purge from its ranks all dishonest and incapable" members, in order to regain the confidence of voters.

Polls carried out by independent newspapers have indicated the nationalist HDZ is likely to lose in the voting for the first time since assuming power in 1990. The party would still retain its parliamentary majority.
